prompt: A flat layered paper-cut collage in a strict handcraft design system: everything is cut from colored cardstock and hanji paper with perfectly clean cut edges — NO outline of any kind on any piece: no bright edge line, no white edge, no dark contour line. Each object is built from two to five completely flat die-cut pieces layered ON THE OBJECT ITSELF — its own silhouette, a main color piece, one or two detail pieces and a highlight piece — the object is never placed on a base, platform, pedestal, plinth or pile of paper sheets; Every upper piece sits slightly RAISED above the piece beneath it, so along EVERY boundary where two different colors meet, the upper piece casts a soft narrow warm dark-brown shadow down onto the lower piece — a gentle embossed paper relief wherever two colors touch, and this relief shadow is the ONLY depth cue. Cut economy: every scissor cut is purposeful and confident — a shape that is straight in the real object is cut with a clean STRAIGHT edge, and curves appear ONLY where the real object is actually curved. No decorative wavy edges, no bumpy wobbly outlines, no gratuitous scalloping on untextured surfaces; a rectangular block is cut as a plain rectangle, though corners may be gently ROUNDED — softly rounding a corner is natural scissor work. Shapes stay simple and chunky, no detail finer than real scissors could cut. Scalloped repeat patterns for textures like straw or waves, cut big and loose. Strictly straight-on orthographic front view, zero perspective. No volume, no curvature, no folded paper, no sculpting. Real-scissors discipline: every piece is a shape that could actually be cut with scissors from a single sheet of colored paper. EACH PIECE IS EXACTLY ONE SOLID FLAT COLOR — no gradient, no shading, no airbrush, no painted detail inside a piece; every color change is a separate stacked paper piece, even a thin line is its own paper strip. ALL pieces share one identical fine colored-paper texture. All shadows are neutral warm dark-brown paper shadows, never colored. A layered paper-cut diorama scene seen straight-on: the scene is built from SIX to EIGHT flat paper layers one behind another (far sky, distant hills, middle ground, ground, near foreground), each layer a cut-paper silhouette casting a soft warm shadow on the layer behind, giving strong depth like a shadow-box. Leave the lower middle of the image open and uncluttered so characters can stand there. Scene: a TOP-DOWN view looking straight down at a warm wooden plank bedroom floor with a soft sage-green oval rug in the middle. No furniture. A FULL-BLEED sheet filling the ENTIRE image edge to edge, no lime green, no characters unless described. Colour mood: soft, muted, warm picture-book pastels with low saturation — cream walls, honey and light wood browns, gentle warm light; never saturated, never dark. IMPORTANT VIEW: a bedroom floor seen from directly ABOVE (top-down bird's-eye view): wooden floorboards and a round rug, with empty space for three beds side by side; NOT a side view of a room. No text, no watermark.
